questions.question: How do stopping distances and crash severity change with vehicle speed?

options.text: They decrease as speed increases.
They are not affected by speed.
They increase as speed increases.

questions.correctAnswerText: They increase as speed increases.
questions.explanation: Higher speeds mean longer stopping distances and more severe crashes.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: A community service group is picking up trash on the highway ahead.
Workers are on or near the road in the work zone ahead.
Children are playing ahead.
There is a pedestrian crosswalk ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Workers are on or near the road in the work zone ahead.
questions.explanation: This sign warns that workers may be on or near the road ahead. Drive carefully through this area.

questions.question: Should you use high beam headlights when driving in fog?

options.text: TRUE
FALSE

questions.correctAnswerText: FALSE
questions.explanation: Use low beam headlights in fog. High beams reflect off the fog and shine back into your eyes, making it harder to see.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: A train station is ahead.
Signal before going further.
Slow down and yield to trains.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and yield to trains.
questions.explanation: This round sign means a railroad crossing is ahead. It is posted a few hundred feet before the tracks. Slow down, look, listen, and be ready to stop.

questions.question: What usually causes hydroplaning?

options.text: Excessive stops.
Sudden stops.
Sudden turns.
Excessive speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Excessive speed.
questions.explanation: At high speeds, your tires cannot clear water from the road. They lose grip and the vehicle slides on a thin layer of water. This is hydroplaning.

questions.question: Must you signal every time you pull away from a curb?

options.text: True
False

questions.correctAnswerText: True
questions.explanation: You must use your turn signal every time you pull away from a curb.

questions.question: How should you avoid hitting vehicles in your blind spots?

options.text: Turn your head quickly to check your blind spot before changing lanes.
Adjust your rearview mirrors every few minutes.
Honk your horn right before turning or changing lanes.
None of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your head quickly to check your blind spot before changing lanes.
questions.explanation: Before turning or changing lanes, turn your head and look over your shoulder to check your blind spot. Do not rely on mirrors alone.

questions.question: When making a turn, you must ____ your speed.

options.text: Increase
Maintain
Vary
Reduce

questions.correctAnswerText: Reduce
questions.explanation: Reduce your speed when turning so you can control your vehicle, stay in your lane, and react to problems.

questions.question: What lights should you use in bad weather or low light?

options.text: Parking lights.
High beams.
Low beams.

questions.correctAnswerText: Low beams.
questions.explanation: Use low beam headlights in fog, snow, or rain. High beams reflect back and cause glare, making it harder to see.

questions.question: What should you do if your vehicle loses traction on wet roads?

options.text: Drive at a constant speed to gain better traction.
Apply the brakes firmly to prevent sliding.
Slow down gradually without using the brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down gradually without using the brakes.
questions.explanation: When hydroplaning occurs, your tires lose contact with the road. Slow down gradually and do not apply the brakes.

questions.question: After passing a vehicle, when is it safe to move back into the right lane?

options.text: After about three seconds.
When you can no longer see the passed vehicle over your right shoulder.
When you can see the entire front of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you can see the entire front of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror.
questions.explanation: After passing, wait until you can see both headlights of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror before returning to your lane. Always check your blind spots before moving back.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Continue at your current speed.
You must stop ahead.
Speeding is not allowed.
There is a traffic signal ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: There is a traffic signal ahead.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that a traffic signal is coming up ahead.

questions.question: If a driver is worried, nervous, angry, or crying, what should they do?

options.text: They will drive the same as usual.
They can drive faster because they are more alert.
They should calm down and focus before starting to drive.
They should call a friend while driving to talk about it.

questions.correctAnswerText: They should calm down and focus before starting to drive.
questions.explanation: Strong emotions like worry, anger, or sadness can distract you from driving. Your mind will not be focused on the road. Take time to calm down and clear your mind before you start driving.

questions.question: If your turn signals fail, what should you use to show you are turning?

options.text: Your horn
Your headlights
Hand signals
Your emergency flashers

questions.correctAnswerText: Hand signals
questions.explanation: If your turn signals do not work, use hand signals to tell other drivers that you are about to turn.

questions.question: Which of the following does NOT happen after drinking alcohol?

options.text: Your reflexes and reaction time slow down.
Your ability to judge speed and distance gets worse.
You become less alert.
You calm down and concentrate better.

questions.correctAnswerText: You calm down and concentrate better.
questions.explanation: Alcohol slows your reaction time, worsens your vision, distorts your judgment of speed and distance, reduces your ability to see in bright light, and lowers your caution about risks.

questions.question: Which statement is true about driving and taking medications?

options.text: Most cold medications can make a person drowsy.
Over-the-counter medications never affect driving if you take the right dose.
Any medication prescribed by a doctor is safe to take while driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Most cold medications can make a person drowsy.
questions.explanation: All medications—whether prescription or over-the-counter—can affect your driving. Cold and allergy medicines can make you sleepy and reduce your ability to drive safely. Know how your medications affect you before you drive.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: No right turn.
Drive only in the direction of the arrow.
Curve ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive only in the direction of the arrow.
questions.explanation: This sign tells you which direction you must drive. You must follow the direction shown by the arrow.

questions.question: What should you do while backing up?

options.text: Rely only on your mirrors.
Flash your lights.
Open your door to see if it is safe.
Turn your head and look out the rear window.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your head and look out the rear window.
questions.explanation: Before backing up, always look behind your vehicle. Children and small objects are hard to see from the driver's seat. Turn your head to look through the rear window while backing. Do not rely only on mirrors or sensors.

questions.question: Large vehicles have blind spots that can extend up to 200 feet behind them.

options.text: TRUE
FALSE

questions.correctAnswerText: TRUE
questions.explanation: Large vehicles have blind spots that extend up to 200 feet behind them. Do not follow closely behind large vehicles because the driver cannot see you.

questions.question: Why does driving at night require extra caution?

options.text: Traffic moves faster at night.
There are more vehicles on the road at night.
Drivers cannot see as well at night.
Accidents happen more often at night.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drivers cannot see as well at night.
questions.explanation: At night, it is dark and you cannot see as far ahead as you can during the day. From 30 minutes after sunset to 30 minutes before sunrise, or whenever you cannot see 500 feet ahead, you must use your headlights.

questions.question: Why do you need extra space in front of a large truck?

options.text: So other drivers can merge onto the freeway.
So the truck driver has room to stop.
So other drivers have space to slow down.

questions.correctAnswerText: So the truck driver has room to stop.
questions.explanation: Trucks are larger than cars. They need more time and distance to stop. Do not pull in front of a truck and then slow down or stop.

questions.question: A pedestrian is walking on the road ahead. An oncoming vehicle is coming toward you. What should you do?

options.text: Slow down and let the oncoming vehicle pass before you pass the pedestrian.
Keep driving at the same speed. The oncoming vehicle must stop for you.
Honk your horn to make the pedestrian move.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and let the oncoming vehicle pass before you pass the pedestrian.
questions.explanation: Handle one hazard at a time. Slow down and let the oncoming vehicle pass first. Then pass the pedestrian if it is safe.

questions.question: When can you drive carefully through an intersection with a yellow light?

options.text: When an emergency vehicle is crossing your lane.
When pedestrians are crossing.
When you are turning right.
When you are already in the intersection when the light turns yellow.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you are already in the intersection when the light turns yellow.
questions.explanation: If the light turns yellow while you are already in the intersection, you may continue through carefully.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: It warns you about road conditions or hazards ahead.
It directs you to cities and towns ahead.
It tells you about traffic laws and rules.
It tells you about road construction ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: It warns you about road conditions or hazards ahead.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are diamond-shaped with black symbols on a yellow background. They warn you about hazards or conditions on the road ahead.

questions.question: Which statement about drinking and driving is true?

options.text: If you can walk straight, it is safe to drive.
If you are under the legal alcohol limit, your driving is not impaired.
Alcohol affects judgment, which you need to drive safely.

questions.correctAnswerText: Alcohol affects judgment, which you need to drive safely.
questions.explanation: Alcohol affects your judgment. Good judgment helps you react safely to things on the road. Even small amounts of alcohol can make driving less safe, even if you are under the legal limit.

questions.question: At a yield sign, you must:

options.text: Yield the right-of-way to traffic that could cause a crash.
Yield only to vehicles on your right.
Slow down but never stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yield the right-of-way to traffic that could cause a crash.
questions.explanation: At a yield sign, let traffic in the lanes you want to enter go first. Be ready to stop, but you can go if the way is clear.

questions.question: You see pedestrians in a crosswalk ahead. What should you do?

options.text: Keep driving. You have the right-of-way.
Wait for the pedestrians to cross.
Drive around the pedestrians to the right.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait for the pedestrians to cross.
questions.explanation: You must yield to pedestrians in a crosswalk. Wait until they cross before driving.

questions.question: When should you allow extra space between your vehicle and the one ahead?

options.text: When following a station wagon.
When following a driver who cannot see behind their vehicle.
When following a small car.

questions.correctAnswerText: When following a driver who cannot see behind their vehicle.
questions.explanation: Drivers of trucks, buses, vans, and vehicles towing trailers cannot see you directly behind them. Stay farther back from these vehicles. This also helps you see around them.

questions.question: When changing lanes, what should you NOT do?

options.text: Check your side and rearview mirrors.
Use your turn signal.
Check for other drivers moving into your lane.
Use your cell phone to call police about the road ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use your cell phone to call police about the road ahead.
questions.explanation: Before changing lanes, check your mirrors, use your turn signal, and check for other drivers. Never use your cell phone while driving to check if the road is clear.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Reduce your speed when the road is wet.
The road has curves and turns ahead.
Traffic will increase ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Reduce your speed when the road is wet.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black symbols. This sign warns you that the road is slippery when wet. Slow down in wet conditions.
